title: The Blue Beetle
paragraphs: Short-lived 1940 juvenile superhero/crime serial adapted from the Blue Beetle comic-book property. Frozen GRH contains both 48 numbered roughly 13-minute installments and 24 paired half-hour presentation objects, yielding 72 archive objects but only 48 underlying serial installments / 24 story pairs.
GRH documents the program through 1940 syndicated Blue Beetle serial (May 15, 1940 to September 13, 1940).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|frank-lovejoy|Frank Lovejoy]] (performer on 15 recordings), Paul Ford (performer on 15 recordings), Charles Nicholas (creator (for all shows)) (performer on 1 recording), and Jean Grombach (performer on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include organized crime and protection rackets, kidnapping, captivity and rescue, crime-fighting gadgets and speculative technology, police work and extra-legal crime fighting, robbery, payroll theft and stolen valuables, and sabotage, espionage and subversion.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Comic-book superhero moves into radio, Juvenile adventure serial culture, Prewar sabotage and spy-story motifs, and Flexible syndicated presentation formats.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|boston-blackie|Boston Blackie]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|box-13|Box 13]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|escape|Escape]] (1 shared credited people), and [[show|lights-out|Lights Out]] (1 shared credited people).
